title: Suspected Endometriosis: Primary Care Recognition and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman, including a young woman aged 17 or under, with symptoms suggesting endometriosis in primary care: recognition, examination, transvaginal ultrasound, first-line analgesia and hormonal treatment, and referral, using NICE NG73.

pathophysiology.summary: NICE advises suspecting endometriosis in women with chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia, cyclical bowel or urinary symptoms, or infertility with other symptoms. A normal abdominal or pelvic examination, ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) does not exclude endometriosis. Serum CA125 is not used to diagnose endometriosis. First-line treatment is a short trial (for example 3 months) of paracetamol or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, with hormonal treatment offered to women with suspected endometriosis.

clinicalManagement.title: Suspect endometriosis
actions: Ask about pelvic pain, dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia, cyclical symptoms and infertility; include young women aged 17 or under.

clinicalManagement.title: Examine
actions: Offer abdominal and pelvic examination; abdominal only if pelvic is inappropriate.

clinicalManagement.title: Consider ultrasound
actions: Consider transvaginal ultrasound even if examination is normal; do not use CA125.

clinicalManagement.title: Start first-line treatment
actions: Trial of paracetamol or an NSAID for about 3 months; offer hormonal treatment such as the combined oral contraceptive pill or a progestogen.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
clinicalManagement.timeframe: If severe, persistent, recurrent or treatment fails
actions: Refer to gynaecology; young women may go to paediatric and adolescent gynaecology or an endometriosis centre.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG73 recommends a short trial (for example 3 months) of paracetamol or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, and hormonal treatment such as the combined oral contraceptive pill or a progestogen (off-label for some products as of September 2017), but gives no doses. Select drug and dose per product information and local protocol. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
